Subject: Clarify data movement + subprocessors for Hosted API — short summary for procurement

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement and Legal have asked for a short, plain-language summary we can include in our internal vendor memo and send to Acme's data mapping team. Specifically they want:

- A two-paragraph explanation of what data the Hosted API processes and whether we (Redwood) transfer any customer-provided content outside of Acme's region.
- A short list of subprocessors (cloud infra, monitoring, analytics) and a one-line statement of the role each plays.
- Any standard safeguards in place for cross-border transfers (SCCs, encryption in transit, narrow KMS access).

If you have a one-pager or a short blurb that sits well in procurement templates, that would be ideal. We prefer plain language rather than legalese.

Also attaching the procurement checklist they sent — they want something simple we can paste into column D.

Appreciate a draft by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,

Hi Liz —

Thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. I put together a short draft below (two paragraphs + subprocessor bullets) and attached an editable one-pager. Please feel free to paste the lines into column D.

DRAFT (plain-language):
Redwood Inference’s Hosted API processes text and related request metadata that customers send to generate responses (for example: prompts, conversation history, and any files you upload as input). We do not use customer-provided content to train models. In most cases, we retain request logs for up to 30 days to support troubleshooting and abuse detection; retention periods can be adjusted for customers with contracts that require different settings.

Some request processing may occur in multiple regions to reduce latency and meet capacity needs. For customers who require data residency, we offer region-specific deployment options and can configure processing to remain within a specified geography. When data crosses borders, we rely on standard safeguards such as EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), encrypted transfer channels (TLS 1.2+), and limited key access controls (customer- or Redwood-managed KMS/HSM where required).

Subprocessors (role):
- Cloud Compute (GPU runtime) — manages model inference workloads and temporary KV cache storage.
- Object Storage (model/artifact storage) — stores model binaries and customer-uploaded artifacts with encrypted-at-rest controls.
- Monitoring & Alerting — collects telemetry and latency/error metrics for platform health (no customer content is used for model training).
- Logging/Observability (aggregated logs) — stores service logs and anonymized telemetry; raw request content is handled per retention settings above.

I’ve flagged a couple of optional sentences depending on how technical you want this to read (see page 2 of the attached one-pager).

Next steps: Laura, can you review the wording for procurement tone? Vanessa/Aisha, can you confirm the subprocessor list and provide the latest export (CSV) we publish for DPA/subprocessor tables? I’ll send to Liz and the Acme team once we align.

Best,
Marcus Lin
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

On Oct 30, 2026, at 11:03 AM, marcus_lin@redwood.com wrote:
> DRAFT (plain-language):
> Redwood Inference’s Hosted API processes text and related request metadata that customers send to generate responses ...

Thanks Marcus — nice, concise. A few procurement-friendly edits below (small copy tweaks to reduce legalese and make bullet points paste-ready). I also suggest a 1-line "what we don't do" callout up front — procurement likes that.

PROPOSED COPY (final to send):
What we don’t do: Redwood does not use customer-provided content to train or improve our public models.

What we do: Redwood’s Hosted API processes the text and metadata customers send to generate outputs (for example: prompts, conversation history, and any uploaded files). We retain request logs for troubleshooting and security; default retention is 30 days, and retention can be shortened by contract.

Where processing may occur: Requests are handled in the customer’s selected region when available. If traffic needs to route to another region for capacity, we will either inform the customer or follow region-limited processing per contract.

Cross-border safeguards: We rely on industry-standard protections: SCCs for EU transfers, encrypted transport (TLS 1.2+), and strict key management controls (customer-managed or Redwood-managed KMS as agreed).

Public subprocessor list (one-line roles for procurement sheet):
- GPU compute (inference runtime)
- Object storage (model/artifacts)
- Monitoring & alerting (platform health only)
- Aggregated logs & metrics (retention-controlled)

Vanessa — please attach the latest CSV with the full subprocessor names + countries. Aisha — would you add the DPA link and a short note about SCCs to the one-pager?

--
Laura Bennett
Head of GTM Contracts — Redwood Inference
